title: Flanagan-Belytschko hourglass control for reduced Hex8
objective: Add the Flanagan-Belytschko hourglass control scheme so reduced-integration Hex8 does not develop zero-energy hourglass modes.
scope: Implement the 4 hourglass basis vectors on the reference Hex8 (the four zero-energy modes of the 1-point rule).
Compute hourglass stiffness = k_h * lambda_h * h^(d-2) / vol_e where lambda_h is user-tunable hourglass control coefficient.
Add the hourglass force and stiffness contribution into the element internal force and tangent kernels.
Follow Flanagan-Belytschko (1981) exactly; reference it in the module docstring.
implementation_steps: Derive / copy the 4 hourglass vectors for the standard Hex8 node ordering.
Compute the hourglass projection of the element nodal velocities.
Add the hourglass force to the internal force assembly.
Add the hourglass stiffness to the tangent matvec.

Unit-test: on a constant-strain problem the hourglass force must vanish. On a patch test of reduced Hex8 (which would otherwise have hourglass energy), the force must now drive the solution correctly.
acceptance_criteria: Hourglass force is zero on a constant-strain state.
Reduced Hex8 patch test passes to 1e-8 with hourglass control on.
Without hourglass control, the same patch test fails (regression guard).

cases: Reduced Hex8 patch test with HG control
Reduced Hex8 patch test without HG control (expected fail)

risks: The classical Flanagan-Belytschko formulation has subtle sign conventions. Mitigation: cite the original paper in the docstring and reference the exact equations used.
completion_notes: Added hourglass.py with 4 HG vectors (xi*eta, eta*zeta, xi*zeta, xi*eta*zeta) derived from HEX8_NODE_COORDS.
Distorted-element correction (gamma projection FB eq. 2.33) ensures AC-1 holds on non-regular hexes.
Two strict-key-equality guards in test_frontend_build_context.py updated to include new key.
Full fast suite: 1182 passed + 16 skipped + 1 expected TODO fail (+4/-4 vs post-P5-4).
